question: On Passage — PROOF Act (H R 10326)
plain_language: This bill requires states to give the Justice Department information it needs to investigate fraud in Medicaid, food assistance, cash welfare, and certain other federal programs, and it limits that data to law-enforcement use. A Yea passes it. A Nay votes no.

question: On Motion to Table — Impeaching Donald John Trump, President of the United States, for high crimes and misdemeanors (H RES 1486)
bill_title: Impeaching Donald John Trump, President of the United States, for high crimes and misdemeanors.
plain_language: The resolution would impeach President Trump over Immigration and Customs Enforcement and Customs and Border Protection practices that it says violate the Constitution. This vote was a motion to table, which kills the resolution. A Yea tables it; a Nay would have left it pending.

question: On Agreeing to the Resolution — Providing for the condemnation and denouncement of socialism in all its forms, and for other purposes (H RES 1490)
bill_title: Providing for the condemnation and denouncement of socialism in all its forms, and for other purposes.
plain_language: This resolution condemns socialism, including the Democratic Socialists of America, and says the House supports the SAVE America Act and elections limited to U.S. citizens. A Yea agrees. A Nay does not.

question: On Motion to Suspend the Rules and Pass, as Amended — Value Over Cost Act (H R 1118)
plain_language: This bill specifies that contracts and orders under the multiple award schedule program of the General Services Administration may be evaluated on best value, rather than lowest overall cost, if the GSA determines that to be in the best interests of the federal government. This vote was under suspension of the rules, so a two-thirds vote was required. A Yea supports passing it as amended; a Nay opposes it.

question: On Motion to Suspend the Rules and Pass, as Amended — Putting Patients First by Strengthening Provider Accountability in FECA Act (H R 8823)
bill_title: Putting Patients First by Strengthening Provider Accountability in FECA Act
plain_language: This bill explicitly authorizes the Department of Labor to suspend payments under the federal workers’ compensation program to certain providers convicted of fraud. This vote was under suspension of the rules, so a two-thirds vote was required. A Yea supports passing it as amended; a Nay opposes it.

question: On Agreeing to the Resolution — Condemning actors seeking to defraud the U.S. Government, and expressing the sense of the House of Representatives that government-wide fraud and improper payment prevention reforms will meaningfully improve the financial prosperity of the U.S., and that Federal program eligibility should be verified before payment (H RES 1335)
bill_title: Condemning actors seeking to defraud the United States Government, and expressing the sense of the House of Representatives that governmentwide fraud and improper payment prevention reforms will meaningfully improve the financial prosperity of the United States, and that Federal program eligibility should be verified before payment.
plain_language: This resolution condemns the actions of those seeking to defraud the U.S. government. A Yea agrees to the resolution; a Nay opposes it.

question: On Passage — Stopping Fraudulent Payments Act (H R 8464)
plain_language: This bill establishes requirements to prevent fraudulent or improper payments from federal programs. A Yea supports passing it in the House; a Nay opposes it.

question: On Motion to Recommit — Stopping Fraudulent Payments Act (H R 8464)
plain_language: H.R. 8464 (Stopping Fraudulent Payments Act) establishes requirements to prevent fraudulent or improper payments from federal programs. A motion to recommit is the minority's last formal chance to send a bill back to committee before the passage vote. A Yea supports sending it back; a Nay keeps it on the floor for the passage vote.

question: On Passage — Fraud Prevention and Accountability Act (H R 8312)
plain_language: This bill assigns improper-payment prevention and spending-transparency functions to the Treasury's Bureau of the Fiscal Service, creates an Office of the Inspector General for Fraud, Accountability, and Recovery within Treasury, and requires Treasury data-sharing agreements with other agencies and allowable private entities to prevent fraud and improper payments. A Yea supports passing it in the House; a Nay opposes it.

question: On Motion to Suspend the Rules and Pass, as Amended — Federal Fraud Prevention Workforce Training Act (H R 8428)
bill_title: Federal Fraud Prevention Workforce Training Act
plain_language: This bill requires the Office of Management and Budget and the Department of the Treasury to establish and maintain a mandatory antifraud and improper payment prevention training program for federal employees whose roles involve federal financial assistance or oversight of federal programs. This vote was under suspension of the rules, so a two-thirds vote was required. A Yea supports passing it as amended; a Nay opposes it.

question: On Motion to Suspend the Rules and Pass — Information Quality Assurance Act (H R 6329)
plain_language: This bill requires the Office of Management and Budget to revise federal agency guidelines for disseminating or using influential information or evidence, meaning information an agency can reasonably determine has a clear and substantial impact on important public actions or private sector decisions. This vote was under suspension of the rules, so a two-thirds vote was required. A Yea supports passing it; a Nay opposes it.

question: On Passage — Veterans Accessibility Advisory Committee Act (S 1383)
bill_title: Veterans Accessibility Advisory Committee Act of 2025
plain_language: This bill carries the Safeguard American Voter Eligibility Act (SAVE America Act) as amended in the Senate; it requires documentary proof of U.S. citizenship to register to vote and photo identification to vote in federal elections. A Yea supports passing it in the House; a Nay opposes it.

question: On Motion to Commit — Veterans Accessibility Advisory Committee Act (S 1383)
bill_title: Veterans Accessibility Advisory Committee Act of 2025
plain_language: As amended in the Senate, S. 1383 carries the SAVE America Act, which requires documentary proof of U.S. citizenship to register to vote and photo identification to vote in federal elections. A motion to commit, like a motion to recommit, is the minority's last formal chance to send the bill to committee before the passage vote. A Yea supports sending it to committee; a Nay keeps it on the floor for the passage vote.

question: On Passage — Disapproving the action of the District of Columbia Council in approving the D.C. Income and Franchise Tax Conformity and Revision Temporary Amendment Act of 2025 (H J RES 142)
bill_title: Disapproving the action of the District of Columbia Council in approving the D.C. Income and Franchise Tax Conformity and Revision Temporary Amendment Act of 2025.
plain_language: This joint resolution reinstates provisions of District of Columbia tax law to conform with federal tax law. A Yea supports passing it in the House; a Nay opposes it.
